description: Persist and delivery-attempt a message to one registered peer selected by peer_id and, when needed, peer_agent_instance_id. For a watcher-held recipient whose derived live binding cannot be reached by its ledger instance ID, pass peer_agent_session_id from peer_list: exact instance resolution remains first, then this stable session key reaches the no-claim watcher binding without inventing a role. The durable delivery channel and the managed-session drive attempt are separate result dimensions. drive_on_delivery is not_managed when a completed lookup proves no managed row, ineligible_state when a managed row is outside the driveable lifecycle states, driver_unavailable when lookup or driver resolution cannot establish a channel, and driver_scheduled when the managed row and its live driver channel resolved and the fixed notice was handed to the bounded delivery-drive executor. The send does not wait for that drive; its finished outcome (driver_sent when the channel accepted the notice, driver_error when it raised) is logged by the solet against the returned message_id. driver_queue_full means the bounded drive queue was at its cap, so no notice was queued; the message itself is still durable. A queued drive re-checks the recipient's lifecycle before touching its pane, so a recipient parked or retired meanwhile logs ineligible_state instead of driver_sent. Neither driver_scheduled nor driver_sent is proof that a model turn started or that the recipient consumed the inbox item. A resolved-but-stale binding fails loud as peer_send_failed after persistence rather than inventing a delivery outcome. The process can also be scheduled as a future durable peer notification.
embedding_description: Send a durable direct peer message by peer id or exact instance, and diagnose the separate managed-session wake attempt. Use when the caller needs the delivery channel plus one of not_managed, ineligible_state, driver_unavailable, driver_scheduled, or driver_queue_full; a scheduled drive is only a queued notice, never model-turn start or inbox consumption.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Returns thread_id, message_id, delivery, resolved recipient identifiers, and drive_on_delivery. delivery describes durable transport routing; queued_* does not prove a turn. drive_on_delivery is exactly one of: not_managed (completed lookup found no managed row), ineligible_state (row exists but its lifecycle is not driveable), driver_unavailable (state or driver channel could not be established), driver_scheduled (the fixed notice was queued on the delivery-drive executor; the send did not wait for it), or driver_queue_full (the drive queue was at its cap; no notice was queued). The finished drive's driver_sent or driver_error is logged against message_id. Neither is evidence of model-turn creation or inbox consumption.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Report the durable delivery channel and drive_on_delivery separately. Never summarize queued_notification, queued_wake, queued_watcher, or driver_scheduled as proof that the peer acted. For not_managed identify the direct target as unmanaged; for ineligible_state name the lifecycle gate; for driver_unavailable flag that no drive was established; for driver_scheduled say only that a driver notice was queued and is not yet confirmed.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Persists a direct peer envelope, attempts bridge delivery, then independently evaluates whether a managed-session driver notice can be sent.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: bridge.not_running means the bridge has not started. peer_send_failed means the resolved peer route is unreachable, its bridge is gone, or its event queue is full; the envelope remains durable. peer_ambiguous means peer_id resolved to multiple live instances without an exact instance hint. The five drive_on_delivery values are successful-result diagnostics, not process errors: not_managed, ineligible_state, driver_unavailable, driver_scheduled, and driver_queue_full.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For peer_ambiguous, select the intended live instance from peer_list and resend with peer_agent_instance_id. For an unreachable direct target, verify its exact binding and use peer_inbox for durable catch-up. If drive_on_delivery is driver_unavailable, or the logged outcome of a scheduled drive is driver_error, retain the delivery receipt but use an independently verified recovery path; a scheduled or sent drive still requires separate evidence before claiming a model turn or consumption.
